sentences.text:
1 3. Brief facts of the case are as under:-
3.1

On 15.02.2005, claimant was driving a motorcycle bearing registration No.
GJ-2AA-1919, owned by opponent No. 3, Mr. Dipakkumar Rameshbhai Dave, who happens to be the real brother of the claimant.
When claimant was passing near Nagalpur Starline Road at around 12:00 to 12:30, opponent No. 1 came on a motorcycle No. GJ-2Q-9262 from behind and collided with the claimant's motorcycle.

As a result of the accident, the claimant sustained injuries and subsequently filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
seeking compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- from the opponents.
3.2. Opponent Nos. 1 & 3 - owners of both motorcycle were served with summons but did not file their written statements.
Opponent No. 2, being the Insurance Company of motorcycle No. GJ-2Q-9262, appeared and filed a written statement at Exh.15.
Opponent No.4, being Insurance Company of motorcycle No. GJ- 2AA-1919 appeared and filed written statement at Exh.16.
Issues were framed.
The claimant filed an affidavit in lieu of examination- in-chief at Exh. 32 and produced documentary evidence in support

NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4978/2010 ORDER DATED: 11/03/2025 undefined of his claim,
namely R.C. book of motorcycle No. GJ-2Q-9262 and the disability certificate issued by neurosurgeon Dr. Mahesh B. Trivedi at Exh.25.
3.3.

After considering the evidence, the learned Tribunal partly allowed the claim petition by dismissing the claim petition against original opponent Nos. 1 & 2, namely the driver-cum-owner and Insurance Company of motorcycle No. GJ-2Q-9262, and directed opponent Nos. 3 & 4, namely the owner and Insurance Company of motorcycle No. GJ-2AA-1919, to pay compensation of Rs.20,460/- with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of the claim petition till realization.
Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation, the claimant-appellant has filed the present first appeal.

4. Learned advocate for the appellant has submitted that learned Tribunal had wrongly dismissed the claim petition against the driver-cum-owner and the Insurance Company of motorcycle No.
GJ-2Q-9262.

It was submitted that claimant, being the real brother of opponent No. 3, was driving motorcycle No. GJ-2AA-1919, and on the date of the accident, the offending motorcyclist hit the claimant's motorcycle from rear side, resulting into serious injuries.

2  C/FA/4978/2010 ORDER DA  
The claimant was admitted in Civil Hospital as an indoor patient for about 10 to 12 days.

sentences.text:
The claimant was working in Loan Department of Maitri Motors and was earning a salary of Rs.2,500/-
per month.
At the time of filing the claim petition, he was working as an insurance agent and was earning Rs.8,000/- per month.
The disability certificate issued by Dr. Mahesh B. Trivedi at Exh.25 indicates disability at 18% of the body as a whole.
The claimant sustained injuries on the left intramural part of his head.

The learned Tribunal did not consider that claimant had agreed to a reduction of disability to the extent of 13% instead of 18%.
5.

Per contra, the learned advocate for respondent No. 2 - the Insurance Company supported the award and pointed out that since the inception of the first appeal, the owner of the motorcycle, Mr.
Dipakkumar Rameshbhai Dave, has remained unserved.
It was further pointed out that owner of the said motorcycle has expired, and no steps were taken by the claimant to bring the heirs of the deceased owner on record.
More particularly, the present respondent No. 3 is the real brother of the claimant.
In view of this fact, the learned advocate for respondent No. 2 - the Insurance Company submitted that the appeal may be dismissed.
C/FA/4978/2010 ORDER DA
6. I have considered the rival submissions and also perused record and proceedings, as well as the paper book produced for consideration.

While deciding the claim application, learned Tribunal considered the documentary evidence, i.e., the R.C. Book of motorcycle No. GJ-2Q-9262, which revealed that the name of the owner was not the same as the person shown in the cause title of the claim application.
Even the policy produced at Exh.28 revealed name of the owner as Ranjeetsingh Dhavalkumar Rameshbhai Dave vs Driver & Owner Of Motor Cycle No ...

3 Gajeshingh Aswal.
Undisputedly, there is no evidence on record to establish that original opponent No.1 was the driver-cum-owner of the said motorcycle.

In the absence of any such material, the learned Tribunal dismissed the claim application against opponent Nos. 1 &
2.

Even during the course of submission, the learned advocate for the appellant could not point out any contrary material from record to persuade this Court to overturn the findings of the learned Tribunal.

6.1. As far as the question of awarding compensation against opponent Nos. 3 & 4, i.e., the owner and the Insurance Company of the offending vehicle No. GJ-2AA-1919, is concerned, the learned Tribunal considered the income of Rs.2,500/- per month in the absence of any documentary evidence.

It was observed by the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4978/2010 ORDER DATED:
11/03/2025 undefined learned Tribunal that Dr. Mahesh B. Trivedi, who certified the claimant's disability, was not examined, and in the absence of any proof of the percentage of disability, the learned Tribunal rightly assessed the disability at 8% of the body as a whole.

Since nothing contrary was pointed out by the learned advocate for the appellant, I do not find any merit in the first appeal,
and therefore, the same deserves to be dismissed and is dismissed accordingly.
7. The record and proceedings, if any, to be sent back forthwith to the concerned Court/Tribunal.
